To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Māori succeed academically in IT and in higher education in general when their identities as Māori and their connections with Māori are valued, affirmed and strengthened.
Māori succeed academically when they have a strong sense of self, when they are connected to their whakapapa (genealogy) and when they feel that they belong.
Māori succeeding at tertiary education are doing so in a context where their Māori identity and cultural capital is a significant element.
In summary, our research is concerned with
Māori succeeding and succeeding well in higher education, and with the development of IT qualifications and field employment.
